# Floating action button — M3 guidance

<!-- Generated by apps/site/scripts/one-off/migrate-guidance.mjs. Do not edit by hand.
     The component pages carry the reference; this file carries the guidance. -->

## Web

### Features

Use one floating action button per screen, for the action a person comes to that screen to perform — composing a message, adding a record, starting a scan. It floats above the content and stays reachable while the screen scrolls. It is emphatic by construction, so it does not need an emphasis variant: if you find yourself wanting a quiet floating action button, the action is probably not the screen's primary one. The extended form carries a label beside the icon when the action would otherwise be ambiguous.

### Usage

**Do**

- Give a screen exactly one fab for its one primary action — compose, add, go.
- Name it with `aria-label` wherever it renders no text (`md`, `large`, `icon`) — a floating button with no name is unusable with a screen reader.
- `lowered` sits the fab quieter at level 1 where the standard level 3 would shout.

**Don't**

- Don't put two fabs on one screen — one primary action means one fab.
- Don't disable a fab — M3 defines no disabled FAB. Hide the action instead of disabling it.
- Don't use a fab for navigation between destinations — that is the navigation bar's job.

### Tokens

| Element | State | Token | Value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Container | resting | comp.fab.container | primary-container, large corners, level3 |
| Container | hover | sys.elevation.level4 | level4 (lifts from level3) |
| Lowered container | resting | sys.elevation.level1 | level1 with the lowered fill swap |

### FAQ

**Which size?**

Default is the standard fab; `sm` compact, `md` and `large` expressive emphasis, `icon` the square for a single glyph. Sizes change the box, never the emphasis.

**Why do the size names differ from native?**

They spell the same five steps differently — web `sm`/`md` vs native `small`/`medium` (`default`, `large`, `icon` match). Same boxes, different spellings; the page names both so the drift is visible, not silent.

## Native

### Features

Reach for a fab when a screen has exactly one action that matters most — compose, add, navigate — and that action should be available without scrolling. Material 3's fab variants are a SIZE axis, not an emphasis axis, so `size` walks small 40, default 56, medium 80 and large 96 plus kern's compact `icon`; `color` walks the seven expressive styles with the container/ink pairing resolved per style. The fab rests at elevation level 3 — it is one of the few components that genuinely floats — and `fabStyles` is exported so the same raised surface can back a custom pressable.

### Usage

**Do**

- Give a screen exactly one fab for its one primary action — compose, add, go.
- Pick the size by emphasis context: default 56 for the standard case, small 40 for compact, medium 80 / large 96 for expressive emphasis.
- `color` defaults to the primary treatment; the six other styles retint without changing the elevation.

**Don't**

- Don't put two fabs on one screen — one primary action means one fab.
- Don't use a fab for navigation between destinations — that is the navigation bar's job.
- Don't ship a fab with no `onPress` — a floating decoration in the wrong place.

### Tokens

| Element | State | Token | Value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Container | resting | theme.color.primaryContainer | primaryContainer (default `primary`), level 3 |
| Ink | resting | theme.color.onPrimaryContainer | onPrimaryContainer label and glyph |
| Container shape | resting | theme.shape.large | large corners (lowered rests at level 1) |
| Surface option | resting | theme.color.surfaceContainerHigh | surfaceContainerHigh with primary ink for the `surface` style |

### FAQ

**Which size?**

Default 56 is the standard fab. Small 40 is compact-only (deprecated for general use); medium 80 and large 96 are expressive emphasis; icon is the 56 square for rails.

**How does this differ from the web fab?**

Same size axis, same seven color styles, same level-3 resting elevation (Android elevation 3dp, iOS quartet to match). The `lowered` treatment rests at level 1 on both renderers.
